report.summary: Chunk 7 of daedalus/spine/attempt.py: defines Attempt properties ok, has_artifact, to_dict, and helper functions pytest_gate_argv, _remove_gate_tmpdir, _poll_until_done.
risks: _remove_gate_tmpdir | medium | Uses remove_tree_no_follow which is not defined in this chunk; could raise NameError if not imported. | Check if remove_tree_no_follow is imported or defined elsewhere in the module.
_remove_gate_tmpdir | low | Catches all exceptions and returns a string; may mask unexpected errors. | Consider whether broad exception handling is appropriate.
_poll_until_done | medium | proc.cancel() is called but its behavior depends on the object type; not defined here. | Verify that proc has a cancel method with expected semantics.

_poll_until_done | low | Uses time.monotonic() but started is a float passed in; potential mismatch if started is not from time.monotonic(). | Ensure started is obtained from time.monotonic() before calling.

handoff.purpose: Defines Attempt properties (ok, has_artifact, to_dict) and helper functions for gate execution (pytest_gate_argv, _remove_gate_tmpdir, _poll_until_done).

symbols.name: has_artifact
symbols.note: Returns True if self.artifact is not None.

symbols.name: to_dict
symbols.note: Returns a JSON-safe dictionary representation of the attempt.

symbols.name: pytest_gate_argv
symbols.note: Returns a tuple of command-line arguments for running pytest as a gate.

symbols.name: _remove_gate_tmpdir
symbols.note: Deletes a temporary directory using remove_tree_no_follow; returns None on success or error string on failure.

symbols.name: _poll_until_done
symbols.note: Polls a subprocess until completion, cancellation, or timeout; returns tuple (cancelled, timed_out, returncode).

claims.text: True only for a real, gated candidate. ``no_change`` is not ok.
claims.why: The property returns self.state == STATE_CLEAN; if state is STATE_NO_CHANGE (assumed elsewhere), it would not be equal to STATE_CLEAN, so the claim holds for this chunk.

claims.text: JSON-safe view. Carries the gate SUMMARY, not the full log.
claims.why: The to_dict method returns a dict with many fields; whether it is 'JSON-safe' depends on the types of all values (e.g., datetime objects). The gate summary is included via self.gates.summary() but the full log is not shown; however, the claim about 'not the full log' is uncheckable because we don't see what the full log would be.

claims.text: The gate command line, as a pure function so it is assertable.
claims.why: The function takes a tuple of paths and returns a tuple of strings; no side effects are visible in this chunk, so it appears pure.

claims.text: ``-p no:cacheprovider`` keeps pytest from writing ``.pytest_cache`` into the candidate worktree; the patch is captured before gates run, but a gate that dirties the tree it is judging is a trap worth not setting.
claims.why: The argument '-p no:cacheprovider' is included, but the claim about its effect (preventing .pytest_cache) and the timing of patch capture are not verifiable from this chunk alone.

claims.text: Delete the gate's scratch directory through the GUARDED walker.
claims.why: The function calls remove_tree_no_follow(tmpdir) but 'GUARDED walker' is not defined in this chunk; we cannot confirm that remove_tree_no_follow is guarded.

claims.text: Returns ``None`` on success, or a one-line report of what stopped it.
claims.why: The function returns None on success (no exception) or a formatted string on exception, which is a one-line report.

claims.text: ``tmpdir`` is ``%TEMP%/daedalus-gate-*``, created while candidate code is running as THIS user with THIS user's privileges, and the prefix is a public constant in this file.
claims.why: The prefix is not shown in this chunk; we cannot verify the path pattern or the existence of a public constant.

claims.text: Candidate code can therefore create paths inside it.
claims.why: This is a logical consequence of the previous claim; not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: Measured on this box (CPython 3.10.11): ``shutil.rmtree`` is safe against a junction that is ALREADY in place, and unsafe against one renamed in mid-walk, because its check reads the Windows ``scandir`` stat cache and never refreshes it -- with the victim in the last entry position it destroyed the target 3/3.
claims.why: This is a claim about behavior of shutil.rmtree on a specific system; not verifiable from this code chunk.

claims.text: THE CONTAINMENT THAT IS NOT WRITTEN DOWN ANYWHERE ELSE, so it is written here: the gate child runs under :class:`daedalus.spine.cancel.ManagedProcess`, i.e. inside a Windows Job Object with ``KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE``, and ``release()`` runs on the ``with`` exit BEFORE this function is reached -- so by the time this deletes, the candidate's test process tree is normally already dead.
claims.why: References to ManagedProcess, Windows Job Object, and release() are outside this chunk; cannot verify.

claims.text: Cerberus could not demonstrate a live candidate at this point (two job-escape attempts failed on this box).
claims.why: Refers to external testing not present in this chunk.

claims.text: That is a reason to believe the window is small; it is not a reason to leave an unguarded recursive delete behind it, because 'the process was probably dead' is not a property this module can check, and a Job Object is not a filesystem guard -- anything the candidate planted while it WAS alive is still on disk when this runs.
claims.why: Reasoning about module properties and Job Object limitations; not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: Poll one gate child, honouring the cancel token and the deadline.
claims.why: The loop checks ctx.is_cancelled() and time.monotonic() > deadline to break, honoring cancellation and timeout.
The function returns a tuple of those three values as seen in the return statement (not fully shown but implied by the code).

claims.text: POLLING RATHER THAN READING IS WHY OUTPUT GOES TO A FILE. With a pipe this loop would have to drain it; a chatty child fills the pipe buffer and blocks while we are asking the cancel token, so the attempt becomes uncancellable at exactly the moment cancelling matters.
claims.why: The claim explains design rationale; we cannot verify that output goes to a file from this chunk alone.

claims.text: Shared by both spawn paths so the contained and uncontained children are cancelled by the same code -- a second copy is a second place for that deadlock to reappear.
claims.why: Refers to spawn paths not present in this chunk.

observations.what: Attempt properties ok and has_artifact are simple boolean properties.
to_dict returns a dictionary with many fields, including artifact.summary() and gates.summary().
pytest_gate_argv is a pure function returning a tuple of strings.
_remove_gate_tmpdir uses remove_tree_no_follow which is not defined in this chunk.
_remove_gate_tmpdir catches all exceptions and returns a string, potentially swallowing errors.
_poll_until_done calls proc.cancel() on cancellation or timeout; proc type is Any, so cancel behavior is unknown.
_poll_until_done uses time.monotonic() for deadline comparison but started is passed as a float; caller must ensure it is from time.monotonic().
